A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same encoder-redundancy study, with matching CUR/IG definitions and identifiable retained experiments. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original encoder-masking experiments, LLaVA-Next fusion comparisons, and model-size analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original masking results and reports additional model evaluations, attention analyses, masking controls, and qualitative examples in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The proposed framework still evaluates encoder subsets through masking and computes the same CUR and IG metrics. Attention analysis and mean-masking are supplementary diagnostics and controls; they do not replace the proposed method or introduce a new architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 15 benchmarks across General, Knowledge, OCR & Chart, and Vision-Centric categories (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 5). The additional model evaluations and chart/counting examples do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Eagle-X4 8B Plus, Eagle2 9B, DeepSeek-VL 7B, and I-MoF 13B to reported full-versus-masked model comparisons; their inclusion in v1's architecture survey was not an evaluated comparison. Conversely, v1's CLIP-only/DINO-only versus LLaVA-SA/LLaVA-CC comparison disappears.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a full-MME attention protocol comparing full models with single-active-encoder variants using KL/JS divergence, correlations, and error metrics. It also adds zero-versus-mean masking controls on MMBench, MMVP, ScienceQA, and TextVQA. Existing exhaustive subset evaluation and benchmark normalization remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine whether attention distributions corroborate encoder dominance, how masking choice affects apparent dependence, and how individual answers change under masking (Tables 2, 4, 16 and Appendix D). The controlled LLaVA-Next fusion experiment in v1 Section 4.2 and Figure 4 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed experiments, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Min/max/mean summarize encoder combinations; the new attention correlations and divergences serve as comparison metrics rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The detailed Eagle-X5 and Cambrian-1 8B masking scores and Cambrian model-size summary are retained. v2 adds substantial results for other models and new analyses, including Eagle-X4's overall IG of 70.27% and single-active-encoder TextVQA scores of 10.67 under zero-masking versus 65.96 under mean-masking (Table 4). v1's LLaVA fusion results are removed.

T1.justification: CUR and max-minus-min IG remain mathematically unchanged. v1's displayed redundancy inequality is replaced by equivalent prose, while v2 Appendix A explicitly writes the existing benchmark-averaging calculation. Neither version supplies substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions—establishing encoder redundancy and introducing CUR/IG—remain intact. v2 adds an explicit measured training-efficiency claim, including 1.69× faster dual-encoder fine-tuning, while removing the introduction's attribution of redundancy to naive fusion and frozen encoders.

C2.justification: v2 replaces much of the fusion/unfreezing explanation with attention-based interpretations and revised arguments about encoder size and pretraining objectives. It adds limitations concerning higher-order encoder interactions and predicting performance before training, while dropping v1's uncertainty about applicability beyond its principal model families. Mean-masking also receives a new interpretation involving preserved prior information.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies do_sample=False, num_beams=1, and max_new_tokens=1024. v2 also documents attention extraction, relates mean-masking to torch.mean, and reports approximately 1700 A100 GPU-hours for five-encoder fine-tuning. These disclosures add reproducibility information without establishing changed settings for retained experiments.

R1.justification: The central positioning against existing multi-encoder models and observations in Eagle/MouSi is retained. v2 removes the token-redundancy subsection and its contrast with methods such as Honeybee, TokenPacker, Deco, FastV, VTW, and PDrop, while adding citations including LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave and Skywork R1V.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experimental setup moves from Section 3.3 to 4.1, benchmark-category descriptions move into Appendix A, the research-question and boxed-finding structures disappear, and Appendix C gains explanatory prose. Author and header information also changes.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column proceedings formatting to a single-column preprint layout. The architecture illustration is replaced, masking plots are consolidated and expanded, CUR tables become comparative bar charts, and new analysis tables and case-study figures appear. Appendix tables are redesigned, including previously rotated displays; the removed model-size plot's numerical summary remains.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's acknowledged uncertainty beyond its main Eagle/Cambrian experiments, v2 supplies broader model evidence, a masking control, and more informative CUR limitations, improving empirical support and transparency. The gain is tempered by removal of the LLaVA fusion study, sparse documentation of timing claims, and new inconsistencies: Tables 2/16 disagree on SAM versus Pix2Struct, and the claimed ≥90% single-encoder retention overlooks Table 3's 13–17% Knowledge losses.
